title: What REALLY Happens If You Fall Into a Black Hole?
sources: Einstein 1915, General Theory of Relativity (Gravitational Time Dilation)
Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019, First M87* Image
Kip Thorne 1994, Black Holes & Time Warps: Einstein's Outrageous Legacy

lines.text: If you fell into a black hole, you would actually watch the future of the universe pass in seconds.
Black holes aren't just cosmic vacuums. They warp space and time to the absolute extreme.
As you get closer, gravity bends light around it, forming a glowing halo called the photon sphere.
Here is where physics gets wild. If a friend watched you from outside, they would never see you enter.
Because gravity slows time, they see your clock ticking slower until you freeze at the edge forever.
Yet from your perspective, you plunge right in, watching billions of cosmic years flash by behind you!
Then, tidal gravity takes over. The pull at your feet is millions of times stronger, stretching you like a noodle!
Inside the horizon, space and time swap roles. Reaching the singularity becomes as unavoidable as tomorrow.
At the center lies the singularity, where infinite mass is crushed to zero volume, and physics breaks down.
Black holes are nature's ultimate time machines. Subscribe to Behind The Science to explore the cosmos!
